correctness.rationale: For finite rooted trees with the reflexive descendant relation, the bounded morphism condition is f(T_x)=U_{f(x)}. Every source child maps to a descendant of the target vertex, and its image cone contains an immediate target child v exactly when its image root is the target vertex or v itself. Inclusion-exclusion over uncovered target children counts the maps exactly and induction on source subtree order proves the recurrence. Amortizing over source edges gives the claimed arbitrary-precision arithmetic-operation complexity. Separate coverage-state, direct-function, and rooted-isomorphism checks corroborate bounded instances; no finite test establishes the all-tree assertion.

originality.rationale: The standard references establish forth/back semantics and modal invariance, not a counting recurrence for arbitrary finite rooted tree pairs. Tree embedding and inclusion results concern different maps; accessible prior special-family counting formulas and existence conditions do not give all-tree multiplicities. Earlier specialized treatment under another terminology remains possible.
residual_risks: Specialized finite modal-frame quotient counting or a general open-map counting formula could imply this recurrence under other terminology.
The prior limited-height and topological-minor results are related but do not prove complete pairwise multiplicities.
This historical self-review is not itself an independent scientific certification.

value.rationale: Counting exact bounded-morphism multiplicities is a natural invariant of finite modal frames; mere existence does not determine it. A recurrence for arbitrary rooted tree shapes, including nonisomorphic source and target, together with fixed-parameter arithmetic-operation complexity in the target branching degree is a meaningful global classification, not a single small table. Star and binary-to-chain specializations expose nontrivial multiplicities. There is no claim of bit-complexity FPT, unrestricted polynomial time, or complexity lower bound.
